records.source: Σκιὰν γὰρ ἔχων ὁ νόμος τῶν μελλόντων ἀγαθῶν, οὐκ αὐτὴν τὴν εἰκόνα τῶν πραγμάτων, κατ’ ἐνιαυτὸν ταῖς αὐταῖς θυσίαις ἃς προσφέρουσιν εἰς τὸ διηνεκὲς οὐδέποτε δύναται τοὺς προσερχομένους τελειῶσαι·
records.gloss: A shadow for having the law of the coming good things, not itself the form of the things, each year with the same sacrifices which they offer to the continuous never is able those approaching to perfect;
pieces: For the law holds only a shadow of the good things to come, not the very form of the things themselves. It can never, by the same sacrifices offered without end each year, make perfect those who approach.

L.1: For the law, having a shadow of the good things to come, not the very form of the things, can never, by the same sacrifices which they offer year after year without end, make perfect those who approach.

R.1: The law of Moses gave only a shadow of the good things God was going to give. It was not the real thing. So the same sacrifices, offered every year, again and again, can never make complete the people who come near to God.

decisions.choice: shadow: an outline cast by something real; form: the reality itself
decisions.reason: σκιά is the shadow an object casts, which shows its outline but not its substance (8:5, "a copy and shadow"; Colossians 2:17). εἰκών usually means an image, but here it stands against "shadow" and means the actual form, the things themselves. The law pointed to the good things to come without containing them.

decisions.choice: not the very form of the things
alternatives: and the form of the things
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads "not the very form". The oldest papyrus of Hebrews instead reads "and the form", which would say the law had both the shadow and the form. Almost all other manuscripts support the SBLGNT reading, and the contrast between shadow and reality fits the argument. This note is written from general knowledge; reviewers must check it against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: it (the law) is able
alternatives: they (the sacrifices or priests) are able
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT has the singular δύναται, with the law as subject. Many manuscripts have the plural, "they can never", making the sacrifices or the priests the subject. The sense is much the same. Reviewers must check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: year by year: the Day of Atonement
decisions.reason: The sacrifices offered "each year" are those of the Day of Atonement (Leviticus 16:34), which the author described in 9:7 and 9:25.

decisions.choice: make perfect: bring to the goal, with a cleansed conscience and full access to God
decisions.reason: As at 2:10, τελειόω means to bring to the goal. For worshipers the goal is a conscience cleansed of sin and free access to God (9:9, 10:2, 10:14). Repeated sacrifices could not do that.

decisions.choice: without end: with "they offer"
alternatives: can never make perfect, for all time
decisions.reason: The phrase εἰς τὸ διηνεκὲς can go with "they offer" (the sacrifices go on and on) or with "make perfect" (they can never perfect anyone for good). It stands next to "they offer", and the repetition of the sacrifices is the point of 10:1-4.

decisions.choice: the very form
decisions.reason: In ordinary use "image" suggests a copy, which is the opposite of what is meant here. "Form" says that the thing itself is present.

decisions.choice: make complete; come near to God
decisions.reason: Readable says "make complete" for "make perfect" here and through the chapter, because "perfect" in everyday speech suggests being without fault. It says "come near to God" for those who approach in worship, supplying "God", whom they approach.

decisions.choice: the law of Moses
decisions.reason: Readable names the law the author means, the law given through Moses with its priests and sacrifices (7:11, 10:28).

records.heading: One sacrifice, once for all

records.source: ἐπεὶ οὐκ ἂν ἐπαύσαντο προσφερόμεναι, διὰ τὸ μηδεμίαν ἔχειν ἔτι συνείδησιν ἁμαρτιῶν τοὺς λατρεύοντας ἅπαξ κεκαθαρισμένους;
records.gloss: Otherwise not would they have ceased being offered, because of none having any longer conscience of sins those serving, once having been cleansed?
pieces: Otherwise, would the offerings not have come to an end? The worshipers, once cleansed, would no longer carry sins on their conscience.

L.2: Otherwise would they not have stopped being offered, because those serving, cleansed once, [would] no longer have any conscience of sins?

R.2: If the sacrifices could make people complete, people would have stopped offering them. Those who worship would have been made clean once and for all. Their sins would no longer weigh on their conscience.

decisions.choice: a question that expects the answer yes
decisions.reason: ἐπεὶ ("otherwise", "since in that case") introduces what would follow if the sacrifices could make worshipers perfect: they would have stopped. The question with οὐκ expects "yes, they would have stopped". That they go on shows they do not do it.

decisions.choice: conscience of sins: an awareness of guilt that stands between the worshiper and God
decisions.reason: συνείδησις is the inner awareness of having done wrong. In Hebrews the problem the sacrifices could not solve is the conscience (9:9, 9:14, 10:22): a worshiper who is truly cleansed no longer carries sins on it.

decisions.choice: those serving: the worshipers; once: once for all
decisions.reason: λατρεύω is to serve God in worship, as in 9:9 and 9:14. ἅπαξ means once, and so once for all, the opposite of the yearly repetition (9:26-28).

decisions.choice: the offerings; the sacrifices
decisions.reason: The Greek verb has no stated subject; Balanced and Readable name the sacrifices of verse 1.

records.source: ἀλλ’ ἐν αὐταῖς ἀνάμνησις ἁμαρτιῶν κατ’ ἐνιαυτόν, ἀδύνατον γὰρ αἷμα ταύρων καὶ τράγων ἀφαιρεῖν ἁμαρτίας.
records.gloss: But in them a reminder of sins every year, \v 4 impossible for blood of bulls and of goats to take away sins.
pieces: Instead, these sacrifices bring sins back to mind every year,
because the blood of bulls and goats cannot take sins away.

L.3: But in them [there is] a reminder of sins every year.
L.4: For impossible [it is for the] blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.

R.3: Instead, each year the sacrifices remind people of their sins.
R.4: The blood of bulls and goats can never take sins away.

decisions.choice: a reminder: sins are brought back to mind
decisions.reason: ἀνάμνησις is a calling to mind. Each year the sacrifices remind the people of their sins instead of removing them. This stands against the promise quoted in 10:17, where God says he will no longer remember them.

decisions.choice: bulls and goats: the Day of Atonement sacrifices
decisions.reason: On the Day of Atonement the high priest offered a bull for himself and goats for the people (Leviticus 16:3, 5-15), as the author has said in 9:12-13.

decisions.choice: for: the reason the reminder goes on
decisions.reason: γὰρ gives the reason the sins are remembered every year: animal blood cannot remove them.

decisions.choice: bring sins back to mind
alternatives: there is a reminder of sins
decisions.reason: Balanced makes the sacrifices the subject so that the sentence reads naturally.

records.source: διὸ εἰσερχόμενος εἰς τὸν κόσμον λέγει· Θυσίαν καὶ προσφορὰν οὐκ ἠθέλησας, σῶμα δὲ κατηρτίσω μοι·
records.gloss: Therefore coming into the world he says: Sacrifice and offering not you desired, a body but you prepared for me;
pieces: That is why, as {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} comes into the world, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says: "Sacrifice and offering {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} did not want, but a body {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have made ready for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

L.5: Therefore, coming into the world, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says, "Sacrifice and offering {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} did not desire, but a body {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} prepared for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}};"

R.5: That is why, when {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} comes into the world, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to God: "You did not want sacrifices and offerings. Instead, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made a body for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

decisions.choice: Psalm 40:7 (39:7 Greek): the Greek reads "a body you prepared for me"
alternatives: ears you have dug for me (the Hebrew)
decisions.reason: Verses 5-7 quote Psalm 40:7-9 (39:7-9 Greek). Here the Greek Psalm, which Hebrews quotes, differs from the Hebrew. The Hebrew says "ears you have dug for me", that is, you have opened my ears to hear and obey. The Greek reads "a body you prepared for me", the whole person given for obedience in place of the part that hears; a few manuscripts of the Greek Psalm have "ears", like the Hebrew. The author's argument rests on the word "body": Christ's obedience was carried out in the offering of his body (10:10).

decisions.choice: the speaker is Christ, entering the world
decisions.reason: The verb has no stated subject; from 9:28 and 10:10 it is Christ. "Coming into the world" refers to his becoming human. The present "he says" treats the psalm as the Son's own words, as the author does with other psalms (2:12).

decisions.choice: prepared: fitted, made ready for a purpose
decisions.reason: καταρτίζω is to put in order or fit for use (11:3, of the ages being prepared by God's word). The body was made ready for the work of doing God's will.

decisions.choice: sacrifice and offering: the offerings of the law
decisions.reason: θυσία is a sacrifice of an animal; προσφορά an offering more generally, including grain offerings. Together they cover the law's offerings, which verse 8 lists in full.

decisions.choice: Christ (the Messiah)
decisions.reason: The Greek verb has no stated subject. Balanced and Readable name Christ, as 9:28 and 10:10 make clear.

decisions.choice: says to God
decisions.reason: Readable says to whom the words are spoken; the psalm addresses God (verse 7).

records.source: ὁλοκαυτώματα καὶ περὶ ἁμαρτίας οὐκ εὐδόκησας.
records.gloss: Burnt offerings and for sin not you delighted in.
pieces: "In burnt offerings and sin offerings {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} took no delight."

L.6: "In whole burnt offerings and [offerings] for sin {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} did not take pleasure."

R.6: "Animals burned whole on the altar, and offerings to take away sin, did not please {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

decisions.choice: burnt offerings and sin offerings
decisions.reason: A burnt offering (ὁλοκαύτωμα) was an animal burned whole on the altar (Leviticus 1). "For sin" (περὶ ἁμαρτίας) is the Greek Old Testament's phrase for the sin offering (Leviticus 5:7, 6:25).

decisions.choice: you did not take pleasure in
decisions.reason: This continues Psalm 40:7 (39:7 Greek). Most manuscripts of the Greek Psalm read "you did not ask for"; Hebrews has εὐδόκησας, "you did not take pleasure in", a word that returns in 10:38. The Psalm also has "burnt offering" in the singular. The sense is the same: God did not want the sacrifices for their own sake.

decisions.choice: animals burned whole on the altar
decisions.reason: Readable explains what a burnt offering was.

records.source: τότε εἶπον· Ἰδοὺ ἥκω, ἐν κεφαλίδι βιβλίου γέγραπται περὶ ἐμοῦ, τοῦ ποιῆσαι, ὁ θεός, τὸ θέλημά σου.
records.gloss: Then I said: Look I have come, in scroll of book it has been written about me, to do, the God, the will of you.
pieces: "Then I said, 'See, O God, I have come to do {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} will, just as the scroll of the book says of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.'"

L.7: "Then I said, 'Look, I have come (in [the] scroll of [the] book it is written of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}) to do, O God, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} will.'"

R.7: "Then I said, 'God, I have come to do {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} will, just as it is written about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in the scroll of Scripture.'"

decisions.choice: Psalm 40:8-9 (39:8-9 Greek), shortened
decisions.reason: The quotation ends with Psalm 40:8-9. The Psalm reads "I desired to do your will, my God, and your law is within my heart". The author stops at "to do your will" and moves "O God" before it, so that the sentence turns on doing God's will, the point taken up in verses 9-10.

decisions.choice: the scroll of the book: the written Scriptures
decisions.reason: κεφαλίς is a roll or the knob at the end of a scroll; with βιβλίου it means the scroll itself. In the Psalm it is the written law; the author reads it of what Scripture says about Christ.

decisions.choice: to do: the purpose of "I have come"
decisions.reason: τοῦ ποιῆσαι gives the purpose of coming. The words about the scroll stand between them as an aside.

decisions.choice: Look; See; (left out)
decisions.reason: Ἰδοὺ draws attention to what follows. Literal and Balanced say "Look" and "See"; Readable leaves it to the sentence. None uses the old word "behold".

decisions.choice: the scroll of Scripture
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly which book is meant.

records.source: ἀνώτερον λέγων ὅτι Θυσίας καὶ προσφορὰς καὶ ὁλοκαυτώματα καὶ περὶ ἁμαρτίας οὐκ ἠθέλησας οὐδὲ εὐδόκησας, αἵτινες κατὰ νόμον προσφέρονται, τότε εἴρηκεν· Ἰδοὺ ἥκω τοῦ ποιῆσαι τὸ θέλημά σου· ἀναιρεῖ τὸ πρῶτον ἵνα τὸ δεύτερον στήσῃ.
records.gloss: Above saying that sacrifices and offerings and burnt offerings and for sin not you desired nor you delighted, which according to law are offered, \v 9 then he has said: Look I have come to do the will of you; he takes away the first so that the second he may establish.
pieces: First {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says, "Sacrifices and offerings, burnt offerings and sin offerings {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} did not want and took no delight in", though these are the offerings the law prescribes.
Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says, "See, I have come to do {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} will." He removes the first in order to put the second in its place.

L.8: Saying above, "Sacrifices and offerings and burnt offerings and [offerings] for sin {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} did not desire, nor did {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} take pleasure [in them]" (which are offered according to [the] law),
L.9: then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has said, "Look, I have come to do {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} will." He takes away the first so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} may establish the second.

R.8: First {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said that God did not want sacrifices or offerings, burnt offerings or offerings for sin, and was not pleased with them, even though the law said to offer them.
R.9: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "God, I have come to do {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} will." So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} takes away the old sacrifices in order to put the doing of God's will in their place.

decisions.choice: above: earlier in the quotation
decisions.reason: ἀνώτερον ("higher up") points back to the first part of the quotation. The author repeats it, putting the nouns in the plural and joining the two lines, so that it can be set beside "I have come to do your will".

decisions.choice: the very offerings the law commands
decisions.reason: The author's comment stresses that the Psalm sets aside the offerings God himself commanded in the law. They were never what God finally wanted (Psalm 51:18-19; 1 Samuel 15:22).

decisions.choice: the first: the sacrifices; the second: the doing of God's will
decisions.reason: πρῶτον and δεύτερον are neuter, so they do not mean the covenants (the word for covenant is feminine). The first is the system of sacrifices the Psalm rejects; the second is the doing of God's will that Christ came to do, by which we are made holy (verse 10).

decisions.choice: takes away; establish
decisions.reason: ἀναιρέω means to take away or abolish; ἵστημι to set up and make stand. One way of approaching God is removed to make room for another.

decisions.choice: removes the first in order to put the second in its place; takes away the old sacrifices
alternatives: takes away the first to establish the second
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps "the first" and "the second"; Readable names them, following the meaning decision on these words.

records.source: ἐν ᾧ θελήματι ἡγιασμένοι ἐσμὲν διὰ τῆς προσφορᾶς τοῦ σώματος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐφάπαξ.
records.gloss: By which will having been sanctified we are through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
pieces: It is by that will that we have been made holy, through the offering of the body of Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, made once for all.

L.10: In which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, once for all.

R.10: Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} did God's will by offering {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own body once for all time. By that will we have been made holy.

decisions.choice: by that will: God's will, which Christ came to do
decisions.reason: θελήματι picks up "your will" in verses 7 and 9. It is God's will, carried out by Christ's obedience in offering his body. It is by this will, done, that believers are made holy.

decisions.choice: sanctified: set apart for God and made clean, fit to approach him
decisions.reason: ἁγιάζω is to make holy, to set apart for God (2:11, 9:13-14). The perfect participle with "we are" describes a state that has been brought about and lasts. Verse 14 adds that those who are made holy are being made holy.

decisions.choice: once for all: with the offering
alternatives: we have been sanctified once for all
decisions.reason: ἐφάπαξ stands at the end of the sentence and most naturally goes with the offering, which is never repeated (7:27, 9:12). The result for believers is also lasting, so the sense comes out much the same.

decisions.choice: the body: the body prepared for him in verse 5
decisions.reason: "The body of Jesus Christ" answers "a body you prepared for me" in the quotation. What replaces the animal sacrifices is the offering of his own body.

decisions.choice: made holy
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "sanctified"; Balanced and Readable say "made holy", the plain meaning of the word.

decisions.choice: Jesus did God's will by offering his own body
alternatives: by that will we have been made holy through the offering
decisions.reason: Readable splits the sentence and says first what Jesus did, then what came of it.

records.source: Καὶ πᾶς μὲν ἱερεὺς ἕστηκεν καθ’ ἡμέραν λειτουργῶν καὶ τὰς αὐτὰς πολλάκις προσφέρων θυσίας, αἵτινες οὐδέποτε δύνανται περιελεῖν ἁμαρτίας.
records.gloss: And every priest indeed stands daily ministering and the same often offering sacrifices, which never are able to take away sins.
pieces: Every priest stands at his duties day after day, offering over and over the same sacrifices, and these can never remove sins.

L.11: And every priest stands day by day ministering and offering many times the same sacrifices, which are never able to take away sins.

R.11: Every priest stands and does his work each day. Over and over he brings the same sacrifices. But they can never take sins away.

decisions.choice: stands: the work is never finished
decisions.reason: μὲν sets up the contrast with verse 12. The priests stand, because their work is never done; Christ sat down, because his is finished. There was no seat for the priests in the tabernacle.

decisions.choice: take away: strip off entirely
decisions.reason: περιαιρέω means to take away something that surrounds or covers, to remove completely. It is a stronger word than the one in verse 4.

decisions.choice: priest
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads ἱερεὺς, "priest". Some important manuscripts read "high priest", perhaps under the influence of 5:1 and 8:3. The daily offerings were made by the ordinary priests, which suits "priest". This note is written from general knowledge; reviewers must check it against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: ministering: performing priestly service
decisions.reason: λειτουργέω is used of priests carrying out their public service in the temple (8:2, 8:6, 9:21).

records.source: οὗτος δὲ μίαν ὑπὲρ ἁμαρτιῶν προσενέγκας θυσίαν εἰς τὸ διηνεκὲς ἐκάθισεν ἐν δεξιᾷ τοῦ θεοῦ, τὸ λοιπὸν ἐκδεχόμενος ἕως τεθῶσιν οἱ ἐχθροὶ αὐτοῦ ὑποπόδιον τῶν ποδῶν αὐτοῦ, μιᾷ γὰρ προσφορᾷ τετελείωκεν εἰς τὸ διηνεκὲς τοὺς ἁγιαζομένους.
records.gloss: This one but one for sins having offered sacrifice in perpetuity sat down at right of the God, \v 13 henceforth awaiting until are placed the enemies of him a footstool of the feet of him, \v 14 by one for offering he has perfected for all time those being sanctified.
pieces: This priest, though, offered a single sacrifice for sins, good for all time, and then sat down at the right hand of God.
From then on {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is waiting for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} enemies to be put under {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet as a footstool.
By that one offering {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has brought those who are being made holy to perfection for all time.

L.12: But this [one], having offered one sacrifice for sins for all time, sat down at [the] right hand of God,
L.13: from then on waiting until {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} enemies are placed [as] a footstool for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet.
L.14: For by one offering {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has perfected for all time those who are being sanctified.

R.12: But Jesus offered one sacrifice for sins, and it works for all time. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sat down in the place of honor at God's right hand.
R.13: Now {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is waiting for God to put {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} enemies under {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet.
R.14: By that one offering {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has made complete forever the people God is making holy.

decisions.choice: Psalm 110:1 (109:1 Greek)
decisions.reason: "Sat down at the right hand" and "until his enemies are placed as a footstool for his feet" come from Psalm 110:1, quoted in 1:13 and echoed in 1:3, 8:1 and 12:2. In Hebrew the speaker of the psalm is the LORD, with the divine name.

decisions.choice: for all time: with the sacrifice
decisions.reason: εἰς τὸ διηνεκὲς can go with "having offered one sacrifice" (a sacrifice good for all time) or with "sat down" (he sat down for good). The SBLGNT has no comma to decide it. Verse 14 uses the same phrase of the effect of the one offering, which favors taking it with the sacrifice; the other reading also fits the contrast with the standing priests.

decisions.choice: has made perfect: as at 2:10, brought to the goal for good
decisions.reason: As at 2:10 and 10:1, τελειόω means bringing to the goal. Here it is done for believers: one offering has cleansed their conscience and given them access to God. The perfect tense marks a finished act whose result lasts.

decisions.choice: those who are being made holy
decisions.reason: The present participle ἁγιαζομένους can describe people in the process of being made holy, or simply name them as "the sanctified" (as in 2:11). Verse 10 says they have been made holy; here their holiness is still being worked out (12:10, 12:14). Both are true in Hebrews.

decisions.choice: are placed: God is the one who puts the enemies under him
decisions.reason: The passive τεθῶσιν leaves the doer unstated; in Psalm 110:1 it is God who makes the enemies a footstool.

decisions.choice: this priest; Jesus
decisions.reason: οὗτος means "this one", the priest of verses 5-10. Balanced says "this priest"; Readable names Jesus.

decisions.choice: the place of honor at God's right hand; for God to put
decisions.reason: Readable explains that the right hand is the place of honor, and names God as the one who puts the enemies under his feet.

decisions.choice: made complete
decisions.reason: As in verse 1, Readable says "complete", because "perfect" in everyday speech suggests being without fault.

records.source: μαρτυρεῖ δὲ ἡμῖν καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον, μετὰ γὰρ τὸ εἰρηκέναι·
records.gloss: Bears witness now to us also the Spirit the Holy, after for the having said:
pieces: The Holy Spirit also bears witness to this for us. For after first saying,

L.15: And the Holy Spirit also testifies to us; for after having said,

R.15: The Holy Spirit also tells us that this is true. First the Spirit says,

decisions.choice: the Spirit speaks in Scripture
decisions.reason: As in 3:7 and 9:8, words of Scripture are presented as the Holy Spirit speaking. The words are Jeremiah's, but the Spirit testifies through them "to us", the readers, now.

decisions.choice: after having said: the sentence runs on into verses 16-17
decisions.reason: "After having said" introduces the first part of the quotation in verse 16. The words that would say what the Spirit then says are not written; they are understood before the second part in verse 17.

decisions.choice: to this; that this is true
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the Spirit bears witness to: what verse 14 has just said.

decisions.choice: the Spirit says
decisions.reason: Readable names the Spirit again so that the speaker of the quotation is clear.

records.source: Αὕτη ἡ διαθήκη ἣν διαθήσομαι πρὸς αὐτοὺς μετὰ τὰς ἡμέρας ἐκείνας, λέγει κύριος, διδοὺς νόμους μου ἐπὶ καρδίας αὐτῶν, καὶ ἐπὶ τὴν διάνοιαν αὐτῶν ἐπιγράψω αὐτούς, καὶ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν αὐτῶν καὶ τῶν ἀνομιῶν αὐτῶν οὐ μὴ μνησθήσομαι ἔτι·
records.gloss: This the covenant that I will covenant with them after the days those, says Lord, giving laws of me upon hearts of them, and upon the mind of them I will inscribe them, \v 17 and the sins of them and the lawless deeds of them not not I will remember any more.
pieces: "This is the covenant I will establish with them when those days are past, says the Lord: I will set {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} laws on their hearts and inscribe them on their minds."
Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} adds, "Their sins and their acts of lawlessness I will not call to mind ever again."

L.16: "This [is] the covenant that I will make with them after those days, says [the] Lord: putting {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} laws upon their hearts, I will also write them upon their mind,"
L.17: [then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says,] "and their sins and their lawless deeds I will by no means remember any longer."

R.16: "Here is the covenant I will make with them when that time comes, says the Lord. I will place {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} laws in their hearts and write them in their minds."
R.17: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says, "I will never again remember their sins and the ways they broke {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} law."

decisions.choice: Jeremiah 31:33-34 (38:33-34 Greek)
decisions.reason: The author quoted Jeremiah 31:31-34 in full in 8:8-12. Here he quotes two parts of it again, freely: "with them" in place of "with the house of Israel", "hearts" before "mind", and the last line of verse 34 joined directly to verse 33. Where the Greek has κύριος, "Lord", the Hebrew has the divine name YHWH.

decisions.choice: the second part of the quotation begins at verse 17
alternatives: the Spirit's main statement begins at "says the Lord"
decisions.reason: The sentence begun in verse 15 ("after having said") needs a second verb, which is not written. It is understood before verse 17: the Spirit first speaks of the covenant, then adds the promise to forget sins. That promise is what verse 18 builds on.

decisions.choice: no added words before verse 17
decisions.reason: Some later manuscripts add words such as "afterward he says" before verse 17, to supply the missing verb. The earlier manuscripts, which the SBLGNT follows, do not have them. This note is written from general knowledge; reviewers must check it against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: by no means will I remember: a strong denial
decisions.reason: οὐ μὴ with the future is the strongest denial Greek has. God's not remembering answers the yearly "reminder of sins" in verse 3.

decisions.choice: lawless deeds: acts that break God's law
decisions.reason: ἀνομία is lawlessness, the disregard of God's law; in the plural, particular acts of it.

decisions.choice: then he says; then he adds
decisions.reason: The verb that introduces the second part of the quotation is understood in the Greek. All three levels supply it; Literal puts it in brackets.

records.source: ὅπου δὲ ἄφεσις τούτων, οὐκέτι προσφορὰ περὶ ἁμαρτίας.
records.gloss: Where now forgiveness of these, no longer an offering for sin.
pieces: And once these have been forgiven, no further offering for sin remains to be made.

L.18: Now where [there is] forgiveness of these, [there is] no longer an offering for sin.

R.18: When sins have been forgiven, people do not need to bring any more offerings for sin.

decisions.choice: forgiveness: release from sins
decisions.reason: ἄφεσις is release, the cancelling of a debt or a wrong (9:22). "These" are the sins and lawless deeds of verse 17.

decisions.choice: no more offering: the conclusion of the argument
decisions.reason: This sentence closes the argument about the priesthood and sacrifice of Christ that began in 7:1. If sins are truly forgiven, nothing further needs to be offered for them.

decisions.choice: remains to be made; people do not need to bring
decisions.reason: The Greek has no verb. Balanced and Readable supply one that says what "no longer an offering" means.

records.source: Ἔχοντες οὖν, ἀδελφοί, παρρησίαν εἰς τὴν εἴσοδον τῶν ἁγίων ἐν τῷ αἵματι Ἰησοῦ, ἣν ἐνεκαίνισεν ἡμῖν ὁδὸν πρόσφατον καὶ ζῶσαν διὰ τοῦ καταπετάσματος, τοῦτ’ ἔστιν τῆς σαρκὸς αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἱερέα μέγαν ἐπὶ τὸν οἶκον τοῦ θεοῦ, προσερχώμεθα μετὰ ἀληθινῆς καρδίας ἐν πληροφορίᾳ πίστεως, ῥεραντισμένοι τὰς καρδίας ἀπὸ συνειδήσεως πονηρᾶς καὶ λελουσμένοι τὸ σῶμα ὕδατι καθαρῷ·
records.gloss: Having therefore, brothers, boldness for the entrance of the holy places by the blood of Jesus, \v 20 which he inaugurated for us a way new and living through the curtain, that is the flesh of him, \v 21 and priest great over the house of the God, \v 22 let us approach with true heart in full assurance of faith, having been sprinkled the hearts from conscience evil and having been washed the body with water pure;
pieces: So then, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, the blood of Jesus has given us confidence to go into the sanctuary.
He has opened for us a way that is new and living, a way through the curtain, which is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} flesh.
And we have a great priest who is over the house of God.
So let us approach with hearts that are true, fully sure in our faith, our hearts sprinkled and cleansed of an evil conscience and our bodies bathed in clean water.

L.19: Therefore, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, having boldness for the entrance into the holy place by the blood of Jesus,
L.20: which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} inaugurated for us [as] a new and living way through the curtain, that is, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} flesh,
L.21: and [having] a great priest over the house of God,
L.22: let us approach with a true heart in full assurance of faith, [our] hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience and [our] body washed with pure water.

R.19: So, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, because of the blood of Jesus we have confidence to go into the holiest place, where God is.
R.20: Jesus opened a new and living way for us through the curtain. That curtain is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own body.
R.21: We also have a great priest who is in charge of God's house.
R.22: So let us come near to God with honest hearts and a faith that is fully sure. Our hearts have been sprinkled clean, so our conscience no longer accuses us, and our bodies have been washed with pure water.

decisions.choice: one sentence: two things we have, then "let us approach"
decisions.reason: Verses 19-22 are one sentence. "Having" governs two things: confidence to enter, and a great priest. On that basis come three calls: "let us approach" (verse 22), "let us hold fast" (verse 23) and "let us consider one another" (verse 24). They answer the summary of 4:14-16.

decisions.choice: the holy place: the inner sanctuary where God is present, here in heaven
decisions.reason: τῶν ἁγίων is the term used in 9:8, 9:12, 9:24-25 for the inner sanctuary, which only the high priest entered once a year. Now all believers may enter it, the true sanctuary in heaven, through Jesus' blood.

decisions.choice: boldness: the freedom and right to come openly
decisions.reason: παρρησία is the freedom to speak and act openly, without fear; in Hebrews it is the confidence of those who come before God (3:6, 4:16, 10:35).

decisions.choice: inaugurated; new and living
decisions.reason: ἐγκαινίζω is to dedicate or open something for use, the verb used in 9:18 of the first covenant. The way is πρόσφατος, newly made, and ζάω, living, because it is the way of the living Christ (7:25), unlike the dead animals of the old sacrifices.

decisions.choice: his flesh is the curtain through which the way passes
decisions.reason: "That is, his flesh" most naturally explains "the curtain": the curtain that closed off the holy place is identified with Christ's body, and the way opened when his body was given in death (compare Mark 15:38, where the temple curtain is torn). Some read "his flesh" with "way" instead: the way is his human life and death. The word order favors the first.

decisions.choice: a great priest over the house of God
decisions.reason: "Great priest" is the Greek Old Testament's name for the high priest (Leviticus 21:10; Numbers 35:25). The house of God is God's people, over whom Christ stands as Son (3:6).

decisions.choice: a true heart: sincere and undivided; full assurance of faith: faith that is fully sure
decisions.reason: ἀληθινῆς καρδίας is a heart that is genuine, holding nothing back. πληροφορίᾳ πίστεως is faith with no doubt left in it, as 6:11 speaks of the full assurance of hope.

decisions.choice: sprinkled and washed: priests made ready to serve
decisions.reason: Priests were washed with water and sprinkled with blood when they were ordained (Exodus 29:4, 29:21; Leviticus 8:6, 8:30), and the people were sprinkled with the covenant blood (9:19-22). Believers are now made fit to come near, inwardly by the cleansing of the conscience (9:14) and outwardly by washing, which may also point to baptism.

decisions.choice: the holy place; the sanctuary; the holiest place, where God is
decisions.reason: The Greek is plural but means the one inner sanctuary. Literal says "the holy place", Balanced "the sanctuary", and Readable explains it as the place where God is.

decisions.choice: several sentences
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable break the long sentence into shorter ones and repeat "so" before "let us approach" to keep the connection.

decisions.choice: his own body; our conscience no longer accuses us
alternatives: his flesh; from an evil conscience
decisions.reason: Readable says "body" for "flesh" and explains a heart cleansed from an evil conscience as one that no longer accuses us of guilt.

records.heading: Let us approach God with confidence

records.source: κατέχωμεν τὴν ὁμολογίαν τῆς ἐλπίδος ἀκλινῆ, πιστὸς γὰρ ὁ ἐπαγγειλάμενος·
records.gloss: Let us hold fast the confession of the hope unwavering, faithful for the one having promised;
pieces: Let us cling to the confession of our hope without bending, for the one who made the promise is faithful.

L.23: Let us hold firmly the confession of [our] hope, unbending; for faithful [is] the one who promised.

R.23: Let us hold on tightly to the hope we have declared, and never let it slip, because God always keeps {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} promises.

decisions.choice: confession: what we openly declare; here the hope we declare
decisions.reason: ὁμολογία is what is said openly and publicly, the faith believers declare (3:1, 4:14). Here it is the confession of hope: the declared expectation of what God has promised (6:18-19).

decisions.choice: unbending: firm, not leaning one way or the other
decisions.reason: ἀκλινής describes something that does not bend or lean. It describes the confession, which is to be kept straight and firm.

decisions.choice: the one who promised: God
decisions.reason: The one who promised is God, whose promise is backed by his oath (6:13-18; 11:11). His faithfulness is the reason to hold firm.

decisions.choice: the hope we have declared; God always keeps his promises
alternatives: the confession of our hope; the one who promised is faithful
decisions.reason: Readable says what the confession is and names God as the one who promised.

records.source: καὶ κατανοῶμεν ἀλλήλους εἰς παροξυσμὸν ἀγάπης καὶ καλῶν ἔργων, μὴ ἐγκαταλείποντες τὴν ἐπισυναγωγὴν ἑαυτῶν, καθὼς ἔθος τισίν, ἀλλὰ παρακαλοῦντες, καὶ τοσούτῳ μᾶλλον ὅσῳ βλέπετε ἐγγίζουσαν τὴν ἡμέραν.
records.gloss: And let us consider one another toward stirring up of love and of good works, \v 25 not forsaking the assembling of ourselves, as custom with some, but encouraging, and so much more as you see drawing near the day.
pieces: Let us also keep one another in mind, so as to rouse each other to love and good works.
Let us not walk away from our own gatherings, as some have made it their practice, but keep urging one another on, and do it more and more as you see the day coming closer.

L.24: And let us keep one another in view, toward a provoking of love and good works,
L.25: not deserting our own gathering together, as [is the] custom of some, but encouraging [one another], and by so much more as you see the day coming near.

R.24: Let us think about how we can move each other to love and to do good things.
R.25: Some people now stay away when believers meet. Let us not do the same. Instead, let us keep encouraging each other, and do it even more as you see the day of the Lord coming closer.

decisions.choice: consider: give careful attention to
decisions.reason: κατανοέω is to fix one's mind on something, as in 3:1, "consider Jesus". Here believers are to pay attention to one another.

decisions.choice: provoking: a sharp stirring, here for good
decisions.reason: παροξυσμός usually means irritation or a sharp quarrel (Acts 15:39). Here the author turns the word to a good purpose: stirring one another to love and good works.

decisions.choice: not deserting the gathering: not staying away from the believers' meetings
decisions.reason: ἐπισυναγωγή is a gathering together; it is used of believers being gathered to the Lord in 2 Thessalonians 2:1. ἐγκαταλείπω is to leave behind or abandon (13:5). Some had stopped meeting with the other believers, perhaps from fear of the suffering described in verses 32-34.

decisions.choice: encouraging: one another
decisions.reason: παρακαλοῦντες has no object; from the context and from 3:13 ("encourage one another daily") it is one another.

decisions.choice: the day: the day of Christ's coming and judgment
decisions.reason: "The day" with no other description is the day of the Lord, when Christ comes and God judges (9:28, 10:27, 10:37; 1 Corinthians 3:13).

decisions.choice: the day of the Lord
decisions.reason: Readable says which day is meant.

decisions.choice: a new sentence for verse 25
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the participles of verse 25 into their own sentence, repeating "let us".

records.source: Ἑκουσίως γὰρ ἁμαρτανόντων ἡμῶν μετὰ τὸ λαβεῖν τὴν ἐπίγνωσιν τῆς ἀληθείας, οὐκέτι περὶ ἁμαρτιῶν ἀπολείπεται θυσία, φοβερὰ δέ τις ἐκδοχὴ κρίσεως καὶ πυρὸς ζῆλος ἐσθίειν μέλλοντος τοὺς ὑπεναντίους.
records.gloss: Willingly for sinning of us after the to receive the knowledge of the truth, no longer for sins remains a sacrifice, \v 27 fearful but a certain expectation of judgment and of fire fury to devour being about the adversaries.
pieces: If we keep on sinning on purpose after we have come to know the truth, there is no sacrifice for sins left for us.
All that remains is a terrifying prospect of judgment and of a blazing fire that will devour those who oppose God.

L.26: For if we keep sinning willingly after receiving the full knowledge of the truth, there no longer remains a sacrifice for sins,
L.27: but some fearful expectation of judgment and a zeal of fire about to devour the adversaries.

R.26: Suppose we know the truth and still choose to keep on sinning. Then there is no other sacrifice that can take away our sins.
R.27: We can only wait in fear for God's judgment and for the fierce fire that will destroy everyone who stands against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: sinning willingly: deliberate, continued sin, here turning away from Christ
decisions.reason: Ἑκουσίως means willingly, by choice, and the present participle ἁμαρτανόντων describes sin that goes on. The law provided sacrifices for sins done unintentionally, but not for sin done "with a high hand" (Numbers 15:27-31). Verse 29 shows what the author has in mind: rejecting the Son of God and his blood, as in 3:12 and 6:4-6.

decisions.choice: knowledge: coming to know the truth
decisions.reason: ἐπίγνωσις is knowledge that recognizes and grasps; "receiving the knowledge of the truth" is coming to believe the gospel (1 Timothy 2:4).

decisions.choice: no sacrifice remains
decisions.reason: Christ's one offering is the only sacrifice that takes away sins (10:12, 10:18). Someone who rejects it has no other to turn to; the old sacrifices cannot help.

decisions.choice: Isaiah 26:11 (Greek): fire will devour the adversaries
decisions.reason: The words echo the Greek of Isaiah 26:11, where zeal and fire devour the adversaries. "Zeal of fire" pictures God's jealous anger as fire (Deuteronomy 4:24, quoted in 12:29; Zephaniah 1:18).

decisions.choice: those who oppose God; everyone who stands against him
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whose adversaries are meant: God's.

decisions.choice: no other sacrifice that can take away our sins
alternatives: no longer remains a sacrifice for sins
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the point is that there is no other sacrifice besides Christ's.

records.heading: A warning against deliberate sin

records.source: ἀθετήσας τις νόμον Μωϋσέως χωρὶς οἰκτιρμῶν ἐπὶ δυσὶν ἢ τρισὶν μάρτυσιν ἀποθνῄσκει·
records.gloss: Having set aside anyone law of Moses without compassions on two or three witnesses dies;
pieces: Whoever disregards Moses' law is put to death without pity, if two or three witnesses testify.

L.28: Someone who has rejected [the] law of Moses dies without pity, on [the word of] two or three witnesses.

R.28: Under the law of Moses, if two or three people testified that someone had rejected that law, the person was put to death. No one showed any mercy.

decisions.choice: Deuteronomy 17:2-7 (and 19:15)
decisions.reason: The law put to death on the word of two or three witnesses anyone who turned to other gods (Deuteronomy 17:2-7); Deuteronomy 19:15 requires two or three witnesses for any charge.

decisions.choice: rejected: set aside, treated as of no account
decisions.reason: ἀθετέω is to set aside or declare void. The case in Deuteronomy 17 is not a small breach but turning from the LORD to other gods, a rejection of the covenant itself.

decisions.choice: without pity
decisions.reason: οἰκτιρμός is compassion or pity; "without pity" means no mercy could be shown once the charge was proved (Deuteronomy 19:21).

decisions.choice: past tense, with the witnesses first
decisions.reason: Readable describes the law as it was applied in the past and tells the steps in order.

records.source: πόσῳ δοκεῖτε χείρονος ἀξιωθήσεται τιμωρίας ὁ τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ θεοῦ καταπατήσας, καὶ τὸ αἷμα τῆς διαθήκης κοινὸν ἡγησάμενος ἐν ᾧ ἡγιάσθη, καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς χάριτος ἐνυβρίσας.
records.gloss: How much do you think worse will be deemed worthy punishment the one the Son of the God having trampled, and the blood of the covenant common having esteemed by which he was sanctified, and the Spirit of the grace having insulted.
pieces: How much worse, then, do you think is the punishment deserved by someone who has trampled on the Son of God, counted as ordinary the blood of the covenant that made such a person holy, and treated the Spirit of grace with contempt?

L.29: How much worse, do you think, a punishment will he be judged worthy of, who trampled on the Son of God, and counted the blood of the covenant by which he was sanctified [as] common, and insulted the Spirit of grace?

R.29: Think how much worse the punishment will be for someone who treats the Son of God like dirt under their feet. That person treats the blood of the covenant, which made them holy, as if it were nothing special. They insult the Spirit who gives grace.

decisions.choice: how much worse: an argument from lesser to greater
decisions.reason: As in 2:2-3 and 12:25, if rejecting the law given through Moses brought death, rejecting what God has given through his Son brings a heavier judgment.

decisions.choice: trampled on: treated with utter contempt
decisions.reason: καταπατέω is to tread underfoot, a picture of scorn.

decisions.choice: counted as common: treated the holy as ordinary, even unclean
decisions.reason: κοινός is common, not holy, and so ritually unclean. The blood of the covenant (9:20, quoting Exodus 24:8) is the holiest thing there is; to count it as common is to treat it as worth nothing.

decisions.choice: he was sanctified: the person who now rejects the blood
alternatives: Christ was sanctified (set apart) by his own blood
decisions.reason: The subject of ἡγιάσθη is most naturally the person being described, who had been set apart as one of God's people by the covenant blood (10:10, 10:14). Some take it of Christ, who was set apart for his work (John 17:19), but nothing in the sentence marks a change of subject.

decisions.choice: the Spirit of grace (Zechariah 12:10)
decisions.reason: "The Spirit of grace" is the Spirit through whom God gives grace; the phrase echoes Zechariah 12:10. ἐνυβρίζω is to insult or treat with arrogant contempt.

decisions.choice: made such a person holy
decisions.reason: Balanced says "made holy", as at 10:10, and "such a person" so as not to make the sentence about men only.

decisions.choice: like dirt under their feet; the Spirit who gives grace
alternatives: trampled on; the Spirit of grace
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of trampling and the phrase "Spirit of grace". It uses "their" and "them" for any person.

records.source: οἴδαμεν γὰρ τὸν εἰπόντα· Ἐμοὶ ἐκδίκησις, ἐγὼ ἀνταποδώσω· καὶ πάλιν· Κρινεῖ κύριος τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: We know for the one having said: To me vengeance, I will repay; and again: Will judge Lord the people of him.
pieces: For we know the one who said, "Vengeance belongs to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; I will pay it back," and who also said, "The Lord will judge {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people."

L.30: For we know the one who said, "To {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} [belongs] vengeance; I will repay," and again, "[The] Lord will judge {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people."

R.30: We know that God said, "I am the one who will punish. I will pay people back for what they have done." God also said, "The Lord will judge {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people."

decisions.choice: Deuteronomy 32:35
decisions.reason: The first saying is Deuteronomy 32:35, in the Song of Moses. Hebrews' wording is not that of the Greek Old Testament ("in the day of vengeance I will repay") but is close to the Hebrew ("vengeance is mine, and repayment") and is word for word the form Paul quotes in Romans 12:19.

decisions.choice: Deuteronomy 32:36 (also Psalm 135:14)
decisions.reason: The second saying is Deuteronomy 32:36, repeated in Psalm 135:14. Where the Greek has κύριος, "Lord", the Hebrew has the divine name YHWH. In the Song of Moses, God judges in favor of his people against their enemies; the author applies the words to God's judging within his own people, of those who reject his Son.

decisions.choice: vengeance: just punishment
decisions.reason: ἐκδίκησις is the righting of a wrong by punishment, the act of a judge, not personal spite.

decisions.choice: God said
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the speaker.

records.source: φοβερὸν τὸ ἐμπεσεῖν εἰς χεῖρας θεοῦ ζῶντος.
records.gloss: Fearful the to fall into hands of God living.
pieces: Falling into the hands of the living God is a terrifying thing.

L.31: [It is] a fearful [thing] to fall into [the] hands of [the] living God.

R.31: It is terrible to fall into the hands of the living God and face {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} judgment.

decisions.choice: fall into the hands: come under someone's power
decisions.reason: To fall into someone's hands is to come under their power. David chose to fall into God's hands because of his mercy (2 Samuel 24:14); here it is falling under his judgment.

decisions.choice: the living God
decisions.reason: God is the living God (3:12, 9:14, 12:22): real and active, who acts and judges.

decisions.choice: and face his judgment
decisions.reason: Readable says what falling into God's hands means here.

records.source: Ἀναμιμνῄσκεσθε δὲ τὰς πρότερον ἡμέρας, ἐν αἷς φωτισθέντες πολλὴν ἄθλησιν ὑπεμείνατε παθημάτων, τοῦτο μὲν ὀνειδισμοῖς τε καὶ θλίψεσιν θεατριζόμενοι, τοῦτο δὲ κοινωνοὶ τῶν οὕτως ἀναστρεφομένων γενηθέντες·
records.gloss: Remember but the former days, in which having been enlightened a great contest you endured of sufferings, \v 33 this on the one hand by reproaches both and afflictions being made a spectacle, this on the other partners of those thus living having become;
pieces: Think back to those earlier days, after you had been enlightened, when you endured a hard contest of suffering.
At times you were mocked and mistreated in front of everyone; at other times you shared the lot of those who were treated like that.

L.32: But remember the former days, in which, having been enlightened, you endured a great contest of sufferings,
L.33: partly being made a public spectacle by insults and afflictions, and partly becoming partners with those who were so treated.

R.32: Remember what it was like in the early days, after God's light first came into your lives. You suffered a lot, but you endured it.
R.33: Sometimes people insulted you and made you suffer in front of crowds. At other times you stood with others who were being treated that way.

decisions.choice: enlightened: brought to know the truth, made believers
decisions.reason: φωτίζω is to give light. As in 6:4 it describes coming to faith, when the light of the truth first shone on the readers.

decisions.choice: a great contest: a hard struggle, as in the games
decisions.reason: ἄθλησις is a contest like those of athletes. The readers held out through it (ὑπομένω, endure, from the same root as "endurance" in verse 36).

decisions.choice: made a public spectacle: exposed to shame as on a stage
decisions.reason: θεατρίζω is to put on show as in a theater. Their sufferings were public, meant to shame them.

decisions.choice: partly ... partly
decisions.reason: τοῦτο μὲν ... τοῦτο δὲ divides the experience into two parts: what they suffered themselves, and their standing with others who suffered.

decisions.choice: after God's light first came into your lives
decisions.reason: Readable explains "enlightened" as the time when they came to faith.

records.heading: Do not throw away your confidence

records.source: καὶ γὰρ τοῖς δεσμίοις συνεπαθήσατε, καὶ τὴν ἁρπαγὴν τῶν ὑπαρχόντων ὑμῶν μετὰ χαρᾶς προσεδέξασθε, γινώσκοντες ἔχειν ἑαυτοὺς κρείττονα ὕπαρξιν καὶ μένουσαν.
records.gloss: Indeed for with the prisoners you sympathized, and the plundering of the possessions of you with joy you accepted, knowing to have yourselves a better possession and abiding.
pieces: You shared in the suffering of those in prison, and when your goods were seized you welcomed it with joy, for you knew that you owned something better, something that lasts.

L.34: For indeed you suffered with the prisoners, and accepted with joy the plundering of your belongings, knowing yourselves to have a better possession, and a lasting [one].

R.34: You cared about the people in prison and suffered with them. When people took away your things, you accepted it with joy. You knew that you had something better that would last forever.

decisions.choice: the prisoners
alternatives: my chains ("you suffered with me in my chains")
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads τοῖς δεσμίοις, "with the prisoners", which has strong and early support and matches 13:3. Many later manuscripts read "with my chains", which makes the author a former prisoner and was read in later centuries as pointing to Paul. A few have other forms. The letter itself never names its author. This note is written from general knowledge; reviewers must check it against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: a better possession, and a lasting one
alternatives: a better possession in heaven, and a lasting one
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "in heaven" after "possession", making explicit what the earlier text leaves implied (compare 11:16). The SBLGNT does not have it. Reviewers must check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: suffered with: shared their suffering by standing with them
decisions.reason: συμπαθέω is to feel and suffer with someone; it is the word used of Jesus in 4:15. Visiting and supplying prisoners was itself a risk (13:3).

decisions.choice: plundering: violent seizure of property
decisions.reason: ἁρπαγή is seizure by force, whether by a mob or by authorities who confiscated the goods of those under suspicion.

decisions.choice: yourselves: you yourselves own something better
decisions.reason: ἑαυτοὺς stresses that the readers themselves have a better possession, one that cannot be taken from them, unlike the goods they lost.

records.source: μὴ ἀποβάλητε οὖν τὴν παρρησίαν ὑμῶν, ἥτις ἔχει μεγάλην μισθαποδοσίαν, ὑπομονῆς γὰρ ἔχετε χρείαν ἵνα τὸ θέλημα τοῦ θεοῦ ποιήσαντες κομίσησθε τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν·
records.gloss: Not throw away therefore the boldness of you, which has great reward, \v 36 of endurance for you have need so that the will of the God having done you may receive the promise;
pieces: So do not let go of your confidence; a great reward comes with it.
What you need is endurance, so that once you have done God's will you may obtain the promise.

L.35: Therefore do not cast away your boldness, which has great recompense;
L.36: for of endurance you have need, so that, having done the will of God, you may obtain the promise.

R.35: So do not lose your confidence in God. It will bring you a great reward.
R.36: You need endurance, the strength to keep going. Then, after you have done what God wants, you will receive what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised.

decisions.choice: do not throw away your boldness
decisions.reason: ἀποβάλλω is to throw off or discard, as one throws off a cloak. παρρησία is the open confidence before God of verse 19 and 3:6, which they showed in the former days.

decisions.choice: reward: payment of what is due
decisions.reason: μισθαποδοσία is a paying back, a reward (11:26) or a just penalty (2:2).

decisions.choice: obtain the promise: receive what was promised
decisions.reason: κομίζω is to receive what one is due, to carry off. "The promise" means what God promised (6:12, 11:13, 11:39).

decisions.choice: confidence in God; the strength to keep going
decisions.reason: Readable says in whom the confidence is placed and explains "endurance".

records.source: ἔτι γὰρ μικρὸν ὅσον ὅσον, ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἥξει καὶ οὐ χρονίσει·
records.gloss: Yet for a little very little, the one coming will come and not will delay;
pieces: For, "In a very short while now, the one who is coming will arrive and will not be slow in coming."

L.37: For "yet a little, how very little [a while], the coming one will come and will not delay;"

R.37: For God says, "Very soon now, the one who is coming will be here. He will not be late."

decisions.choice: Isaiah 26:20 (Greek) and Habakkuk 2:3 (Greek)
decisions.reason: "A little, how very little" comes from the Greek of Isaiah 26:20. The rest is Habakkuk 2:3-4 in Greek. In the Hebrew of Habakkuk 2:3 it is the vision that "will surely come and will not delay"; the Greek says "he will come", a person. Hebrews adds the article, "the coming one", a title for the Messiah (Matthew 11:3), and so reads it of Christ's return (9:28).

decisions.choice: a very little while
decisions.reason: μικρὸν ὅσον ὅσον is an emphatic way of saying "a very short time".

decisions.choice: For God says
decisions.reason: Readable says who speaks, since verse 38 continues in God's voice ("my righteous one").

records.source: ὁ δὲ δίκαιός μου ἐκ πίστεως ζήσεται, καὶ ἐὰν ὑποστείληται, οὐκ εὐδοκεῖ ἡ ψυχή μου ἐν αὐτῷ.
records.gloss: The but righteous of me by faith will live, and if he shrinks back, not takes pleasure the soul of me in him.
pieces: "But {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} righteous one will live by faith; and if he turns back, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} soul finds no delight in him."

L.38: "And {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} righteous [one] will live by faith; and if he draws back, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} soul does not delight in him."

R.38: "My righteous one will live by faith. But if he turns back, I will not be pleased with him."

decisions.choice: Habakkuk 2:4 (Greek), its two halves reversed
decisions.reason: This is Habakkuk 2:4. The Hebrew reads "the righteous will live by his faithfulness", the faithfulness of the righteous person. The Greek Old Testament reads "the righteous will live by my faithfulness" (God's), or in some manuscripts "my righteous one will live by faith", which Hebrews follows. Hebrews also reverses the two halves of the verse, so that the one who may draw back is "my righteous one" himself, a warning to the readers. The line about drawing back follows the Greek; the Hebrew says "his soul is puffed up, not upright in him".

decisions.choice: my righteous one
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads "my righteous one" (μου after δίκαιός). Some manuscripts put "my" after "faith", as in the Greek Old Testament, and some leave it out, as Paul does in Romans 1:17 and Galatians 3:11. This note is written from general knowledge; reviewers must check it against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: faith: trust that holds on until the promise comes
decisions.reason: πίστις here is trust in God that keeps going, the faith described in chapter 11, set against drawing back.

decisions.choice: draw back: shrink back, withdraw in fear
decisions.reason: ὑποστέλλω is to draw back or withdraw, as Peter withdrew from eating with Gentiles out of fear (Galatians 2:12).

decisions.choice: my soul: I myself
decisions.reason: "My soul" is a Hebrew way of saying "I", with the stress on the whole self.

decisions.choice: I will not be pleased with him
alternatives: my soul takes no pleasure in him
decisions.reason: Readable puts the idiom "my soul" as "I".

records.source: ἡμεῖς δὲ οὐκ ἐσμὲν ὑποστολῆς εἰς ἀπώλειαν, ἀλλὰ πίστεως εἰς περιποίησιν ψυχῆς.
records.gloss: We but not are of drawing back to destruction, but of faith to preserving of soul.
pieces: But we are not people who draw back and are lost; we are people of faith, and our lives will be kept safe.

L.39: But we are not of drawing back to destruction, but of faith to [the] preserving of [the] soul.

R.39: But we are not people who turn back from God and are destroyed. We are people who have faith, and our lives will be kept safe.

decisions.choice: of drawing back, of faith: belonging to these kinds of people
decisions.reason: The genitives ὑποστολῆς and πίστεως say what the readers belong to or are marked by: not drawing back, but faith. They pick up the two words of the quotation in verse 38.

decisions.choice: preserving of the soul: life kept safe
decisions.reason: περιποίησις is keeping safe or gaining possession (1 Thessalonians 5:9; Ephesians 1:14). ψυχή is the life or self. Faith leads to life kept safe, as drawing back leads to ἀπώλειαν, destruction.

decisions.choice: people who draw back; people of faith
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply "people" to make the genitives clear.
